title: Zero
logline: Branch A finale, ten in the morning: at the DSP's zero-crime press conference Nandini hands over the impostor in cuffs, as ordered, then reads FIR number one into the microphones, naming the chief guest. Thirty FIRs put Bhaiyaji and her own SHO in custody, the grain stays gone and she says so, she withdraws her transfer application, and straight after the press conference she returns Nirala's salute through the grille of a prison van.
language_note: en-IN: Indian English, same cast as the Hinglish cut. Thana, FIR, almirah, madam, sahab, ji and Bhaiyaji are kept as they are said in India.

characters.name: Nandini Joshi
characters.role: LEAD. Sub-Inspector, Imlipur thana, six weeks into her first posting. She has kept the DSP's order and brought thirty FIRs he did not order.
characters.look: Indian woman, 28, tall (about 170 cm), lean, very straight-backed, long neck. Medium-brown skin, oval face, straight thick black eyebrows, level dark-brown eyes, a firm mouth that rarely smiles. Black hair with a clean centre parting pulled into a low ponytail that reaches her shoulder blades; no fringe, no loose strands. No make-up, no bindi, no jewellery, no watch. PERIOD 1: the approved force uniform, crisp and new: sandy khaki shirt with a pointed collar and two buttoned chest pockets, full sleeves buttoned at the wrist, sharp pressed creases; dark teal epaulettes with TWO off-white bars each; white lantern on a round teal patch on each upper sleeve; khaki trousers; black belt with a black handcuff pouch on her right hip; black shoes; a blue ballpoint pen clipped in her left chest pocket. No cap, no name tag, no stars. NO HELMET anywhere in this episode (D-016 direction 19). In b1 and b2 one steel cuff is locked on her LEFT wrist, chained to Nirala's right; from the end of b2 her wrists are free.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Female, late twenties, clear mid-range voice. Neutral educated north-Indian English with a light small-city Hindi accent; crisp police words; keeps thana, FIR, madam and sir. Not British, not American. Quick and clipped by habit; in front of the microphones she reads like an officer making entries: level, exact, never louder. Under pressure she gets quieter, not louder. Dry, not sarcastic. Her two sentences at the van (l26) are the only soft ones in the episode, fully voiced, never whispered.

characters.name: Sudhir Nirala
characters.role: The man who ran the fake thana. Her prisoner, brought to the press conference in his own uniform; he leaves in the prison van the same morning.
characters.look: Indian man, 40, slight and short (about 160 cm), narrow sloping shoulders, thin neck, a chest that does not fill a shirt. Light-brown skin, long narrow face, large earnest eyes, a neat black pencil moustache, clean-shaven chin. PERIOD 1: a home-stitched copy of the force uniform, over-starched and ONE SIZE TOO BIG: the shoulder seams droop past his shoulders, the sleeves end at his knuckles, the collar stands away from his neck, the trousers are belted high with the tail of the black belt hanging loose. Teal epaulettes with three off-white bars; lantern sleeve patches. THE ONLY PEAKED CAP IN THE SERIES: a khaki peaked cap with a teal band and a shiny black peak, no badge, worn dead level. ONE THING TOO MANY: a single home-made medal pinned above his left chest pocket: a blank brass-yellow disc as wide as his palm hanging from a broad maroon-and-off-white striped ribbon. His holster is EMPTY in this episode (the wooden revolver was booked as case property in s2a01) and the revolver is not in any frame. Cuff state: b1 and b2 his RIGHT wrist is cuffed to Nandini's left; from the end of b2 to the end of b6 the cuff stays on his right wrist and Pushpa holds the free half; in the van (b10, b11) no handcuffs are in view. Red file (thick_file): clamped under his LEFT arm from b1 to b6, as at the end of s2a02; not in view in b10. Cap: dead level b1 to b6; in b10 shots 1 and 2 knocked a finger's width askew by the van door (peak tilted to picture-left) until her fingers set it level in shot 3.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Male, forty, light careful tenor. Careful, slightly old-fashioned Indian English as learnt from manuals, with a small-town north-Indian Hindi accent; complete sentences, no contractions; police terms said with great care. Not British, not American. Courteous, never raises his voice, never jokes. In b6 he speaks to Bhaiyaji as an equal for the only time: formal, steady, not triumphant. At the van he reports his decision like a clerk.

characters.name: Pushpa Kumari
characters.role: Head Constable, Imlipur thana. Holds the second almirah key, Nirala's chain, and in the end the thana's front bench.
characters.look: Indian woman, 50, short (about 152 cm) and solid, round shoulders, strong forearms. Wheat-brown skin, round face, sharp small eyes over round steel-rimmed spectacles worn low on her nose. Grey-streaked black hair in a tight high bun with TWO STEEL KNITTING NEEDLES pushed through it in a cross. Approved force uniform: khaki full-sleeve shirt, teal epaulettes with ONE off-white bar, lantern sleeve patches, khaki trousers, black shoes. Over it, always, a hand-knitted plum-purple cardigan, open at the front, with two sagging pockets; a ball of orange wool shows in the right pocket. In b5 she holds up the small steel almirah key on its loop of orange wool. No cap.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Female, fifty, low, dry, even alto. Plain, unhurried small-town Indian English with a clear Hindi accent; short sentences, the important thing in the fewest words; keeps madam and SHO sahab. Not British, not American. Never surprised. Her lines here (l10, l19, l27) are said completely straight; the warmth in the last one is only dryness.

characters.name: Dayashankar Tripathi
characters.role: Inspector, SHO Imlipur. Two years of zero crime under his shield; thirty refused FIRs and last night's truck on his signature.
characters.look: Indian man, 56, large, heavy and slow, about 175 cm, a big soft belly straining his shirt. Warm-brown skin, bald dome with a fringe of grey hair at the sides, heavy jowls, clean-shaven, half-closed sleepy eyes. Approved force uniform worn slack: khaki half-sleeve shirt with the top two buttons open over a white vest, teal epaulettes with three off-white bars, lantern sleeve patches, khaki trousers. A red-and-white checked gamchha always over his LEFT shoulder. A paper cone of roasted peanuts in his left hand until b8, where it lies on the floor. No cap.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Male, mid-fifties, deep, slow, comfortable baritone. Slow Indian English with a heavy Eastern-UP Hindi accent, never crisp; keeps the Hindi filler 'arre'. Not British, not American. Under pressure he does not shout: he stops chewing, goes low and fast, and blames someone. One line in this episode (l09).

characters.name: Balram 'Bhaiyaji' Thakur
characters.role: The town strongman, the DSP's chief guest this morning, and the accused in all thirty FIRs.
characters.look: Indian man, 45, broad and solid, about 178 cm, thick neck, big square hands. Brown skin, thick black hair combed straight back, a full black moustache, an unhurried closed-lip smile that is his resting face. A spotless white cotton kurta with the sleeves pushed up his forearms over white pyjama trousers; brown leather sandals. A heavy gold watch on his LEFT wrist. A fat ring of godown keys hooked on his RIGHT index finger. A marigold garland round his neck (chief guest; prop per D-016 direction 19). Dark sunglasses pushed up on top of his head in b1; from his name in b4 to the end of his scenes they sit on his nose (the bible's one exception for this episode). He is not seen after b6 shot 4; in b8 shot 1 his marigold garland and the ring of godown keys lie on the seat of the empty chief-guest chair.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Male, mid-forties, warm, low, smiling voice. Soft, hospitable small-town Indian English with a Hindi accent; keeps 'sahab'. Not British, not American. Courteous to the point of menace; he never hurries and laughs before he says the worst thing. One line here (l13), cut off.

characters.name: Anil Rathore, DSP
characters.role: The sub-division's DSP, holding his press conference for Imlipur's second zero-crime year. Never named aloud; addressed as 'sir', 'DSP sir' or 'DSP sahab', never by name.
characters.look: Indian man, 48, tall (about 182 cm) and lean, upright, quick. Brown skin, short silver-grey hair with a side parting, a trimmed grey moustache, rimless rectangular spectacles. Approved force uniform, sharply pressed: khaki full-sleeve shirt, teal epaulettes each carrying ONE BROAD off-white band (no bars, no stars), lantern sleeve patches, khaki trousers, a polished brown belt, a slim brown leather cane tucked under his LEFT arm. No cap.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Male, late forties, bright, quick, clipped baritone; always half addressing the press. Fluent, brisk officer's Indian English with a light north-Indian accent. Not British, not American. Into the microphones he is a showman; aside (l05, l22) he drops to a low, quick voice. Under pressure he pauses once (b7), then pivots smoothly.

characters.name: Reporter (unnamed)
characters.role: One voice from the press, off screen. The only time the press is heard as a person.
characters.look: Never seen. Voice only. Hands holding small recorders at the bottom edge of frame in b4 shot 3 are S7's call; no face, no audience in frame.
characters.voice_note: Same actor as the Hinglish cut. Young, quick, a little too loud; a Hindi-belt TV reporter's quick Indian English. Not British, not American. Gender is the casting director's call. One line (l08), not through the PA.

location: One series plate: real_thana, dressed for the press conference (a table with a cluster of microphones facing camera, a blank cloth banner behind, no audience in frame, no flags, emblems or portraits). The prison van in b10 is a close insert of a barred grille in a blue-grey van door, not a plate. b11 is on the real_thana plate from inside, looking out through the front doorway (D-016 direction 15).
time_of_day: Morning, 10 a.m.: flat warm daylight from the doorway. b10 and b11 are the same morning, straight after the press conference; no time jump.

beats.action: OPENS MID-SPEECH on a squeal of microphone feedback. Shot 1 (the 0.8 s silence and the first half of l01): tight on the microphone cluster; the DSP behind it, picture-centre, mid-word, cane under his left arm; the blank banner behind (overlay ov_press_banner); at the picture-right edge Bhaiyaji in a chair, marigold garland, sunglasses on top of his head, keys on his right finger. Tripathi is only a slack khaki belly, a gamchha edge and a hand with a peanut cone at the picture-left edge behind the DSP: no face. Shot 2 (from 'zero crime', by about 4 s, the hook image): the thana's front doorway in daylight behind them; Nandini (picture-left, the green FIR register held against her chest with her right arm) and Nirala (picture-right, cap level, medal on, the red file under his left arm) step forward together from beside the doorway onto the open floor before the press table, his right wrist chained to her left (the chain runs between them at waist height). Two sheet faces per shot at most.

lines.speaker: dsp
lines.text: [excited] Imlipur thana: second year running, zero crime.

beats.action: Shot 1 (l02): DSP single at the microphones, beaming, his right hand thrown out towards the doorway (cane still under his left arm). Shot 2 (l03): Nandini and Nirala two-shot, she picture-left, he picture-right, the chain between them; she answers like a report. Shot 3 (the silence after, insert, hands only, same sides as shot 2): on picture-left her khaki-sleeved hand turns the key in the cuff on her other wrist, the cuffed wrist nearer picture-centre; the chain runs off picture-right to his wrist; a plum-cardigan sleeve (Pushpa) enters from the top of frame and takes the opened cuff. The other cuff stays on Nirala's right wrist; the red file stays under his left arm.

lines.speaker: dsp
lines.text: [laughs] And here is our fake Inspector: arrested. Well done, SI Joshi.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [flatly] Order carried out, sir.

beats.action: Shot 1 (the silence and l04): Nandini single at the press table; she sets the heavy green register down among the microphones and says what it is. Shot 2 (l05): DSP close, his right hand closed over the head of the nearest microphone, smile fixed, leaning to her, low.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] And this: last night's thirty FIRs.

lines.speaker: dsp
lines.text: [quietly] Not now, Joshi.

beats.action: Shot 1 (the silence, l06 and l07 up to 'Balram Thakur'): Nandini single leaning to a microphone he has not covered, the register open, her finger on the first line (overlay ov_fir_numbers: 1 in the margin); the DSP's hand on the other microphone at the frame edge, hand only. Shot 2 (from 'alias Bhaiyaji' to the end of l07): Bhaiyaji close: the smile holds, but the sunglasses have slid off the top of his head onto his nose. Shot 3 (l08): the table from the press side, the ring of microphones, at the bottom edge two hands holding small recorders (S7's call); the DSP behind them, caught. The camera shutters stop dead after 'extortion' and the reporter's question lands in the hole.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] FIR number one.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [flatly] Accused: Balram Thakur, alias Bhaiyaji. Offence: extortion.

lines.speaker: reporter
lines.text: [excited] DSP sir, the chief guest is the accused?

beats.action: Shot 1 (l09): Tripathi single; he has stopped chewing, peanut cone sagging in his left hand, his right hand jabbing at the register. Shot 2 (l10): Pushpa single, holding up the small steel key on its loop of orange wool, needles crossed in her bun. Shot 3 (l11): Nandini single at the microphone, reading from the page. Shot 4 (l12): over Nandini's shoulder (back of her head and ponytail, no face) to Tripathi, gamchha on his left shoulder; she says it to him.

lines.speaker: tripathi
lines.text: [sharply] Arre, that register was locked in the almirah!

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [deadpan] Second key, SHO sahab.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] All thirty have the same line: 'SHO Tripathi refused to register the FIR.'

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] And last night eight hundred sacks went out on your signature.

beats.action: Shot 1 (l13): Bhaiyaji single, sunglasses on his nose, leaning towards the DSP (a khaki shoulder and the cane tip at the frame edge, no second face), keys swinging on his right finger; Nirala cuts him off. Shot 2 (l14 and l15 up to 'the officer is real.'): Nirala and Pushpa two-shot, he picture-right, cap level, medal on, the red file still under his left arm, the cuff on his right wrist and its free half in Pushpa's hand; he faces Bhaiyaji off picture-left, formal and steady. Shot 3 (from '[quietly] I was the only fake.' through l16): Nirala single, closer; the quiet confession lands on the close single (S4 cuts mid-line at the full stop, as in b4). Shot 4 (the silence after): Bhaiyaji single; the keys have stopped swinging.

lines.speaker: bhaiyaji
lines.text: [chuckles] DSP sahab, on a fake Inspector's papers—

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [earnest] The papers are not mine, Bhaiyaji.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] The register is real, the thumbprints are real, the officer is real. [quietly] I was the only fake.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] And your twenty-four envelopes: case property.

beats.action: Shot 1 (the 2.0 s silence, held): DSP close, his hand still on the microphone, eyes moving behind the rimless spectacles: one pause, one calculation, the shutters going. Shot 2 (l17): he lifts his hand off the microphone and leans into it, the press smile back: he takes the credit. Shot 3 (l18): DSP and Pushpa two-shot, he turned to her (she picture-right), his cane pointing off picture-left towards Bhaiyaji's chair and the SHO's desk; her hands are empty (she has locked Nirala's cuff to a window bar off screen; see writer_notes state lines in script.hi.json).

lines.speaker: dsp
lines.text: [calm] And from today, Imlipur police is taking action in these thirty cases.

lines.speaker: dsp
lines.text: [sharply] Head Constable. Bhaiyaji and SHO Tripathi: take them both into custody.

beats.action: Shot 1 (the silence, insert, no face, low angle): Tripathi's paper cone on the floorboards, roasted peanuts rolling out, his slack trouser legs and shoes beside it; behind, the empty chief-guest chair, the marigold garland and the ring of godown keys left on its seat. Both exits are in the picture. Shot 2 (l19): Pushpa lifts the zero-crime shield off its nail (overlay ov_shield) and lays it face down on the SHO's desk; Tripathi's bulk soft at the frame edge, a shoulder and the gamchha, no face. Shot 3 (l20, l21): Nandini and DSP two-shot at the press table, she picture-left; she does not let him round it up.

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [deadpan] Zero is not zero any more, SHO sahab.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] And the eight hundred sacks won't come back, sir.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] They left right in front of me.

beats.action: The room emptying, as sound and objects only: Shot 1 (the silence and l22): the press table with half the microphones gone and a cable hanging; by the SHO's desk the DSP and Nandini, two-shot, she picture-left, he picture-right; he taps a paper in an open file, aside, as a kindness. Shot 2 (l23, insert, hands only, same sides): the open file held by his hand at picture-right; her khaki-sleeved hand, entering from picture-left, draws the paper out of it. Shot 3 (l24): Nandini single, the paper folded in her hand, the face-down shield on the desk behind her.

lines.speaker: dsp
lines.text: [calm] Your transfer application, Joshi. Shall I sign it today?

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [calm] I am withdrawing it, sir.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [flatly] There are thirty FIRs pending here.

beats.action: THE SAME MORNING, straight after; no plate, close inserts only. Shot 1 (l25): the barred grille of a blue-grey van door, Nirala behind it, his cap knocked a finger's width askew by the van door, peak tilted to picture-left, medal on, still in his uniform, no handcuffs and no red file in view; he says it like a clerk reporting a decision. Shot 2 (first sentence of l26): tight close on Nandini's face seen through the bars, soft daylight behind her, no yard detail. Shot 3 (second sentence of l26, insert): her khaki sleeve with the lantern patch reaches through the bars and her fingers set his tilted cap level, the peak now square. Shot 4 (the silence after, grille insert): he salutes through the grille, right hand to the peak, the cap dead level.

lines.speaker: nirala
lines.text: [calm] I will plead guilty, madam. The uniform was fake.

lines.speaker: nandini
lines.text: [quietly] The work was real. Keep your cap straight.

beats.action: FINAL IMAGE, one held shot on the real_thana plate from inside, looking out (D-016 direction 15). Foreground: the complainants' bench, occupied for the first time: three pairs of hands holding papers, one holding a folded stamped receipt, no faces. Mid-ground: the front doorway in daylight; in it Nandini, straight-backed, three-quarter back to camera, returning the salute towards the yard of her own will, nothing on her wrist. Pushpa's voice from inside, near camera (l27). She holds the salute through the silence as the van's engine is heard pulling away.

lines.speaker: pushpa
lines.text: [calm] Madam, the bench is full.

sfx_notes: Bed, b1 to b9: the real thana by day, full of press that is never seen: a low murmur, camera shutters in bursts, the slow ceiling fan, a scooter far off in the yard. Keep the murmur under every line and drop it a step under the PA lines.

b1: microphone feedback squeal on frame one, about half a second, cut short by a tap on the mic; a burst of shutters; two sets of footsteps in the doorway with a faint chain clink. l01 is through the PA: light room reverb, fully intelligible.
b2: shutters burst on 'Well done'; after l03, the dry click of the cuff unlocking and a short chain rattle as it changes hands.
b3: the heavy register thumps down among the microphones (a small PA pop); a muffled thud as the DSP's palm covers a mic head before l05. l05 is off the PA, close and dry.

b4: l06 and l07 through the uncovered mic, PA reverb kept light. A page turns before l06. The shutters stop dead after 'extortion' and leave a breath of near-silence (fan only) under the speaker change; l08 comes off screen, dry and a little hot, not through the PA.
b5: a small jingle of the steel key on its wool under l10; a page under l11.
b6: Bhaiyaji's keys chink faintly under l13 and stop after l16. Nothing loud on l15.
b7: shutters going steadily through the 2.0 s silence, then thinning as the DSP leans back into the PA for l17.
b8: peanuts pattering across the floorboards in the silence; the shield scraping off its nail and a soft wooden knock as it lands face down, after l19 starts, not on its first words.
b9: the murmur thinning to nothing, cables pulled, a chair scraped; fan; paper slide under l23.
b10: outdoor morning: crows, a far handpump, a dog once. The van door bangs shut BEFORE l25, never under it. Bed low under l25 and l26.
b11: inside room tone, the bench creaking once. l27 sits on a clear bed. Only after l27 has finished: the van's engine turns over and pulls away across the yard, fading through the 3.0 s hold.
music_note: No music from b1 to b6: the shutters and the PA are the score. A single low sustained note enters under the silence at the head of b7 and holds under the DSP's pivot. Out for b8 and b9. A small warm theme, one instrument, enters on Shot 4 of b10 (his salute), ducks right down under l27 and rises a little into the engine fade and the end.
ending_question: The bench is full in daylight, and the man who taught Imlipur to come forward is riding a van to plead guilty: can the real thana keep the trust an impostor earned?
writer_notes: S5 English adaptation of script.hi.json (the version after its 26 Nov review), not a literal translation. Same beats, same speakers, same order, same line ids (l01 to l27), same emotion tags in the same places, same silent_seconds and silent_position per beat. action, on_screen, location, sfx_notes and music_note are the Hindi file's, with one change: where they quote a Hindi cue word for a shot cut or a sound, the English cue word replaces it ('Balram Thakur', 'alias Bhaiyaji', 'extortion' in b4; 'the officer is real.' and '[quietly] I was the only fake.' in b6, cut at the full stop; 'Well done' in b2's sound note). State lines, overlays, faces per frame and props are as written in script.hi.json writer_notes; the picture is shared.

Register (bible en registers, D-016): Nandini crisp and level, with contractions where an officer would use them; Nirala manual-learnt English with no contractions ('The papers are not mine', 'I will plead guilty'); Pushpa short and plain; Tripathi slow, keeps 'Arre' (l09, which also carries the blame in the Hindi 'तो'); Bhaiyaji soft, keeps 'sahab'; the DSP brisk and fluent. Address: Nandini and the reporter say 'sir' or 'DSP sir' to the DSP, as Indian police and press do in English; Bhaiyaji says 'DSP sahab'; Pushpa says 'SHO sahab' and 'madam'; Nirala says 'madam' and 'Bhaiyaji'. The Hindi file's rule of always naming the rank is kept wherever the rank tells a cold viewer who is meant (l08, l10, l11, l13, l18, l19).

Line choices: l03 'Order carried out' is how an officer reports an order done. l05 is 'Not now, Joshi.' rather than 'Later, Joshi.' so the aside is not a two-word turn. l11 uses the Indian legal phrase 'refused to register the FIR'. l12, l20: 'sacks' for बोरी, the same word both times. l13 is cut off after a whole word ('papers—'): end it on the dash and start l14 with no gap. l14 keeps the papers echo with l13. l15 keeps the three-part parallel as full sentences, in Nirala's register, then lands on 'fake'. l25 and l26 keep the fake and real echo of वर्दी नक़ली थी / काम असली था. Nothing was added that is not in the Hindi line, apart from 'our' (l02, the DSP's showman claim) and 'Arre' (l09).

Length (hand count, no tool: this session has no shell). English dialogue is about 1,199 characters, counted as code points with spaces and punctuation, without tags, the space after a tag or speaker labels; likely error a few per cent. English runs more characters than Devanagari for the same words, so this is not comparable with the Hindi 1,050 measure in D-016 direction 7; the comparable figure is the time.

Timing: 27 lines, spoken targets 101.9 s (about 11.8 characters a second, deliberately slow because Gate 0b measured real v4 takes running 20 to 60 per cent over their targets; nothing padded), 15.4 s of silent beats, 17 speaker changes at 0.3 s (5.1 s): 122.4 s, against 131.1 s for the Hindi. Lines more than 15 per cent short of their Hindi target: l05 (1.5 against 1.8 s) and l23 (2.2 against 2.8 s); l18 is at 15 per cent (5.6 against 6.6 s). None is long. Each is covered by its shot's held picture or the silence that follows; the timeline follows measured audio in each language (D-014 rule 6), so no line was lengthened to match.

Subtitles (D-014: at most two lines of 32 graphemes): l11 (about 73 characters), l15 (89), l17 (70) and l18 (71) will not fit one cue. Split l11 at the colon, l15 at 'I was the only fake.', l17 after 'And from today,' and l18 after 'Head Constable.'.

Tags: [excited], [laughs], [calm], [quietly], [sharply] and [chuckles] were used in the proof scenes. [flatly] (l03, l07, l24), [deadpan] (l10, l19) and [earnest] (l14) are in the skill's verify group and are not confirmed for any Series 2 English voice; if a voice ignores one, S10 swaps [flatly] or [deadpan] for [calm] and [earnest] for [calm]. l07 is the climax line and rests on [flatly]: check it first. Casting tried [curt] on Nandini's English voice with no obedience check recorded; if S10 confirms it, l20 may become '[curt] And the eight hundred sacks won't come back, sir.'. Nothing is whispered. [sharply] on l09 and l18 means low and fast, not loud.

Short-turn flags for the voice director: l05 'Not now, Joshi.' (15 characters), l06 'FIR number one.' (15) and l03 'Order carried out, sir.' (23) are short: record extra takes. l27 is the last line: fully voiced, off screen, on a clear bed.

Pronunciation dictionary candidates for the English voices: Imlipur (IM-lee-poor), thana (THAA-naa), Nandini (NUN-di-nee), Joshi (JO-shee), Nirala (ni-RAA-laa), Tripathi (tri-PAA-thee), Pushpa (PUSH-paa), Balram (bul-RAAM), Thakur (THAA-koor), Bhaiyaji (BHAI-yaa-jee), sahab (SAA-hub), almirah (al-MEE-raa), arre (UH-ray), FIR (eff-eye-arr, letter by letter; plural FIRs).
Ending: a resolution episode (ladder rung 6, no cliffhanger). The last spoken line supports the final image and answers nothing in ending_question.

Not verified: the JSON has not been parsed by a tool (no shell this session; ids, speakers, order and tag lists checked by eye against script.hi.json). No line has been voiced or timed; all character counts and targets are by hand.
